text: Every real tattoo starts as a single line on paper.
The artist draws it, and redraws it, until every curve sits right.
A purple stencil carries the design onto clean skin.
Then, the machine. Its needles strike up to three thousand times a minute.
asr: Then, the machine. Its needles strike up to 3,000 times a minute.

text: Each stroke leaves ink about one and a half millimeters below the surface.
Too shallow, and it fades. Too deep, and it blurs.
Down here, the body's own cells catch the pigment, and hold it in place.
Linework first. Then shading. Then color.
asr: Line work first, then shading, then color.

text: In about two weeks, the surface heals over.
And the line from that first page stays for life.
